About this analysis record

This page reads the reviewed stored frames, tables, model-check outputs, figures, and file identities for display. It does not repeat model fitting or scientific computation. In particular, it does not fit or refit a model, generate model predictions, estimate residual correlation, rerun a sensitivity analysis, resample, or simulate.

figureAlt: Two-panel distribution display for near-eye and chest one-hour melEDI. Positive values span a broad right-skewed range on an axis that is linear from zero to one lux and logarithmic above one lux. The adjacent panel shows that exact zeros comprise about 28 to 29 percent of fitted hours.

Two-panel dot matrix of four day-type and activity combinations across nine near-eye and eight chest sites: Borås (SE), Delft (NL), Dortmund (DE), Tübingen (DE), Munich (DE), Madrid (ES), Izmir (TR), San José (CR), and Kumasi (GH). Every primary near-eye site has observations in all four combinations, though some free-day sedentary cells are sparse. Chest data are absent for Tübingen (DE). Point sizes show supported hours, shapes distinguish support categories, and colours identify sites.

Two-panel line chart of supported participant-hours at each local clock hour. Work-day Active hours are most numerous, followed by Free-day Active hours; Sedentary categories have fewer observations. Support remains present across all 24 clock hours at both placements.
figureCaptions: Figure 1: Observed one-hour melEDI in the primary frames. Panel A summarizes positive observations using the 10th–90th percentile line, 25th–75th percentile thick line, median point, and open 99th-percentile point on a true symlog axis. Panel B shows the share of exact-zero hours retained in the models.

Figure 2: Observed participant support for each joint day-type and activity category by study site and placement. Point size represents supported hours; crosses mark cells without observations and open circles mark observed cells with fewer than four participants or eight participant-days. Colours identify sites only.

Figure 3: Supported participant-hours across local clock time for the four joint day-type and activity categories. Colour and line type jointly identify category; panels separate near-eye and chest. The display describes fitted-row support rather than an exposure effect.

The occurrence basis check remains a warning: its k-check p-values are small, although effective degrees of freedom remain below the basis ceiling. The lower-basis comparison changes some response-scale curves. Together with occurrence calibration, residual working correlation, and omitted cross-component covariance, this prevents confirmatory whole-curve inference. Active/Sedentary and Free/Work contrasts are response-scale pointwise displays with null ratio 1. A pointwise 95% CI applies to one displayed hour, not to the whole curve; filled points only indicate that the interval at that hour excludes 1. They are neither simultaneous bands nor multiplicity-controlled whole-curve tests.
